title: Ethical research
log: 2026-10-29T12:14:28Z write: the API refused it in the chapter request, so it is written on its own next

draft.title: Ethical research
card: People agree to take part after they are told what the research is for and what they will be asked to do. They can say no, and they can withdraw later.
The researcher keeps what people share private. Names and details that could identify them are not made public.
The research must not hurt people physically, emotionally or socially. The researcher plans ahead to lower any risk.
The researcher treats participants and their cultures, beliefs and values with dignity. Participants are people to work with, not just sources of data.
draft.remember: Ethical research protects the people in it: they choose to join, stay private, are kept safe and are treated with respect.

a.q: Which action shows that a researcher has gained informed consent?
opts: Explaining the study and letting each person choose to join
Removing students' names before the report is published
Choosing questions that will not upset anyone in the group
Describing a community's customs in a fair and polite way
a.why: Informed consent means people know what the study involves and freely agree, and can withdraw. Removing names is confidentiality, which is tempting but protects privacy after the information is collected, not the choice to take part.
a.clue: Think about what people are told before they agree.

b.q: Priya interviews teenagers in Penrith about bullying. She tells them the purpose, lets them leave at any time, and then names one student and her school in her report. Which ethical principle has she broken?
opts: Avoiding harm in the interview questions
b.why: Naming a student and her school makes it possible to identify her, so Priya did not keep the information confidential. Informed consent is the tempting wrong answer, but Priya did explain the purpose and let students leave, so she met that principle.
b.clue: Look at what happened to the information after the interviews.

a.best: Explaining the study and letting each person choose to join
